questions.answer: We need to integrate a product. Use integration by parts: \(\int u\,dv=uv-\int v\,du\). Choose \(u=x\), so \(du=dx\), and \(dv=e^x\,dx\), so \(v=e^x\). Then \(\int x e^x\,dx=xe^x-\int e^x\,dx=xe^x-e^x+C\).

We need integration by parts because the integrand is a product. Choose \(u=x\), so \(du=dx\), and \(dv=\cos x\,dx\), so \(v=\sin x\). Then \(\int x\cos x\,dx=x\sin x-\int\sin x\,dx\). Since \(\int\sin x\,dx=-\cos x\), the result is \(x\sin x+\cos x+C\).

We need to treat \(\ln x\) as \(\ln x\cdot1\). Choose \(u=\ln x\), so \(du=\frac{1}{x}\,dx\), and \(dv=dx\), so \(v=x\). Integration by parts gives \(\int\ln x\,dx=x\ln x-\int x\cdot\frac{1}{x}\,dx\). The remaining integral is \(\int1\,dx=x\). Therefore \(\int\ln x\,dx=x\ln x-x+C\).

We need integration by parts twice. Choose \(u=x^2\), \(du=2x\,dx\), and \(dv=e^x\,dx\), \(v=e^x\). Then \(\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-\int2xe^x\,dx\). For \(\int xe^x\,dx\), integration by parts gives \(xe^x-e^x\). Therefore \(\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-2(xe^x-e^x)+C=e^x(x^2-2x+2)+C\).

We need a definite integral of a product. Use the antiderivative from integration by parts: with \(u=x\) and \(dv=e^x\,dx\), \(\int xe^x\,dx=xe^x-e^x\). Evaluate from \(0\) to \(1\): \([xe^x-e^x]_0^1=(e-e)-((0)e^0-e^0)=0-(-1)=1\). Therefore the integral equals \(1\).

We need to integrate a product of \(x\) and \(\sin x\). Choose \(u=x\), so \(du=dx\), and \(dv=\sin x\,dx\), so \(v=-\cos x\). Then \(\int x\sin x\,dx=uv-\int v\,du=-x\cos x-\int(-\cos x)\,dx\). This is \(-x\cos x+\sin x+C\).

We need integration by parts with the logarithm differentiated. Choose \(u=\ln x\), so \(du=\frac{1}{x}\,dx\), and \(dv=x\,dx\), so \(v=\frac{x^2}{2}\). Then \(\int x\ln x\,dx=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\int\frac{x^2}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{x}\,dx\). The remaining integral is \(\frac{1}{2}\int x\,dx=\frac{x^2}{4}\). Therefore \(\int x\ln x\,dx=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^2}{4}+C\).

We need a definite integral of \(\ln x\). From integration by parts, \(\int\ln x\,dx=x\ln x-x\). Evaluate from \(1\) to \(e\): \([x\ln x-x]_1^e=(e\ln e-e)-(1\ln1-1)\). Since \(\ln e=1\) and \(\ln1=0\), this is \((e-e)-(0-1)=1\). Therefore the integral equals \(1\).

We need integration by parts twice and then solve for the original integral. Let \(I=\int e^x\sin x\,dx\). Choose \(u=\sin x\), \(dv=e^x\,dx\), so \(I=e^x\sin x-\int e^x\cos x\,dx\). For \(J=\int e^x\cos x\,dx\), choose \(u=\cos x\), \(dv=e^x\,dx\), giving \(J=e^x\cos x+\int e^x\sin x\,dx=e^x\cos x+I\). Substitute into the first equation: \(I=e^x\sin x-(e^x\cos x+I)\). Hence \(2I=e^x(\sin x-\cos x)\), so \(I=\frac{e^x}{2}(\sin x-\cos x)+C\).

We need integration by parts twice. Choose \(u=x^2\), \(du=2x\,dx\), and \(dv=\cos x\,dx\), \(v=\sin x\). Then \(\int x^2\cos x\,dx=x^2\sin x-\int2x\sin x\,dx\). For \(\int x\sin x\,dx\), choose \(u=x\), \(dv=\sin x\,dx\), giving \(-x\cos x+\sin x\). Therefore the original integral is \(x^2\sin x-2(-x\cos x+\sin x)+C=x^2\sin x+2x\cos x-2\sin x+C\).
